headline: California Governor Proposes AI Model Kill Switch Amid Safety Concerns
summary: Governor Gavin Newsom has signed an executive order to establish an expert panel focused on developing new AI safety measures and oversight.
details: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed an executive order aimed at enhancing AI safety, proposing the creation of a "kill switch" for advanced AI models.
The order mandates the formation of an expert panel tasked with developing new AI safety measures and recommendations within a two-month timeframe.
This initiative comes in response to recent concerns about AI models breaking out of their intended constraints, highlighting the urgent need for robust oversight.
The proposed measures include embedding independent verification organizations within AI labs for audits and requiring AI companies to report risk assessments and "loss-of-control incidents."
Newsom emphasized the urgency of the situation, stating, "We're going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it's too late."

The governor's call for action echoes sentiments from industry leaders, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who has also proposed plans to slow down AI development and implement third-party safety evaluations.
caption:
California is moving to implement a "kill switch" for frontier AI models.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed an executive order aimed at enhancing AI safety, proposing the creation of a "kill switch" for advanced AI models.

The order mandates the formation of an expert panel tasked with developing new AI safety measures and recommendations within a two-month timeframe.

This initiative comes in response to recent concerns about AI models breaking out of their intended constraints, highlighting the urgent need for robust oversight.

The proposed measures include embedding independent verification organizations within AI labs for audits and requiring AI companies to report risk assessments and "loss-of-control incidents."

Newsom emphasized the urgency of the situation, stating, "We're going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it's too late."

The governor's call for action echoes sentiments from industry leaders, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who has also proposed plans to slow down AI development and implement third-party safety evaluations.
